name: CA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent John Garamendi running with large financial advantage
Republican challenger minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 97%
model.rationale: Garamendi holds a seat that leans Democratic by 19 points, has a $1.2 million war chest against a challenger with $235 on hand, and faces no outside spending against him. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or unexpectedly strong national Republican wave could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
John Garamendi, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a northern California district that voted Democratic by 19 points at the presidential level. He enters the general election with roughly $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Rudy Recile has raised about $20,000 and reports only $235 in cash, with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Garamendi about a 97% chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided financial gap makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with the only real question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
